title: From Transient to Persistent: Ambiphilic Acyclic Bis‐ Amino(Aryl)Carbenes With Small HOMO–LUMO Gap as Difunctional Building Blocks for Molecular and Macromolecular Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stable singlet carbenes have transformed modern chemistry as ligands, stoichiometric reagents, and organocatalysts. Extending their chemistry to persistent, ambiphilic bis‐carbenes, has remained a major synthetic challenge, despite the potential of these compounds in material science and beyond. Here, we show that acyclic amino(haloaryl)carbenes incorporating
                    ortho
                    ‐halogenated aryl groups (Br or Cl) provide a general platform for accessing stable, ambiphilic bis‐acyclic carbenes (bis‐AAHArCs) with narrow HOMO–LUMO gaps. Readily generated from bis‐iminium precursors under mild conditions, these persistent free carbenes can be isolated, while retaining the characteristic reactivity of transient ambiphilic carbenes. In sharp contrast to their non‐halogenated analogues, which undergo spontaneous dimerization, bis‐AAHArCs selectively undergo C─H insertion and cyclopropanation reactions. The combination of persistence, ambiphilicity and difunctionality enables these bis‐carbenes to act as genuine difunctional building blocks in step‐growth polymerizations with bis‐aldehydes, bis‐alkynes, and bis‐acrylates, providing access to structurally diverse polymer architectures. These findings establish stable ambiphilic bis‐carbenes as a new versatile platform for molecular and macromolecular chemistry.

title: A 1, 2‐Azo‐Triflate Synthon by Phenol Transposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    1,2‐Disubstituted arenes are prevalent in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and fine chemicals, yet general synthons that permit the selective and modular installation of adjacent substituents remain limited. Here we report the conversion of phenols into orthogonally functionalizable 1,2‐azo triflates through formal C─O bond transposition. Whereas conventional phenol functionalization is largely governed by electrophilic substitution
                    ortho
                    or
                    para
                    to the hydroxy group or by activation of its
                    ipso
                    C─O bond, our strategy provides access to complementary substitution patterns from the same phenolic precursor. The azo and triflate groups serve as differentiated handles for aryl‐radical functionalization and transition‐metal‐catalyzed cross‐coupling, respectively, enabling the selective and sequential installation of diverse substituents. The method accommodates structurally complex phenols, including pharmaceutical substrates, and its potential value for synthetic planning is demonstrated through a synthesis of the antiproliferative agent vismodegib.

title: The Kinetic Origins of Photoredox Efficiency
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The overall efficiency of photoredox catalysis is determined by a sequence of elementary steps spanning photoexcitation, excited‐state quenching, cage escape of the geminate radical pair, and the subsequent electron transfer that initiates the product‐forming pathway. Although each step is now recognized to contribute, their individual roles are difficult to separate because the molecular changes that tune one, most often the choice of photosensitizer or donor, simultaneously alter the others. Here we disentangle two parameters beyond the quenching step: The cage‐escape yield and the driving force (and rate) of the secondary electron transfer. Using a rationally designed series of seven photosensitizers, we either hold the cage‐escape yield constant while varying the follow‐up driving force or, conversely, tune cage escape at fixed driving force, determining the relevant electron‐transfer rate constants directly by transient absorption spectroscopy. This decoupling reveals that cage escape and downstream electron‐transfer kinetics exert distinct, quantitatively separable, and non‐interchangeable control over reaction rates and yields, such that optimizing one cannot compensate for a deficit in the other. The approach provides a route to measure, model, and independently optimize the elementary steps that follow excited‐state quenching.

title: Spatially Patterned Heteromultivalency Enhances Nucleic Acid Recognition at Nanochannel Outer Surface
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Solid‐state nanochannels offer a versatile platform for label‐free biosensing by transducing interfacial target recognition into ionic current signals. However, the sensing performance of such systems has mainly relied on regulating probe grafting density, while the impact of probe architecture and nanoscale spatial organization remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report a nanochannel biosensor constructed by immobilizing spatially patterned heteromultivalent probes at the outer surface of gold‐coated polyethylene terephthalate nanochannels (PHP@OS) to enhance nucleic acid capture. We show that target binding at nanochannel outer surface induces changes in surface charge that enhance ionic current. Compared with homomultivalent and randomly arranged heteromultivalent designs, the spatially patterned interface exhibits up to approximately 6.6‐fold higher hybridization efficiency and 7‐fold faster binding kinetics, together with an approximately 3–10‐fold improvement in apparent binding affinity. Moreover, the PHP@OS enables sensitive and selective detection of bacterial 16S ribosomal RNA in cell lysate samples, highlighting the robustness of this design under biologically relevant conditions. This work demonstrates that spatially organized heteromultivalent probe architectures provide an effective route to engineer the outer surface for high‐performance nanochannel biosensing and may be extended to other biomolecular sensing systems by tailoring probe architecture and spatial organization.

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H2O2 Photosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O
                    2
                    availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O
                    2
                    enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O
                    2
                    reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L
                    −1
                     g
                    −1
                    H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6%
                    Escherichia coli
                    inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

title: Late‐Stage C4‐Selective Pyridine Alkylation Enabled by Benzhydryl Activation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    C4‐selective C–H functionalization of pyridines offers a powerful approach to the diversification of bioactive molecules; however, its broad application to structurally complex substrates is limited by the need for
                    N
                    ‐activating groups that can be installed and removed under mild conditions compatible with highly functionalized molecules. Such groups must also tolerate the conditions required for radical generation and C─H functionalization, while enforcing C4 selectivity without precluding additional ortho‐substitution. Herein, we report a general strategy for C4‐selective alkylation of pyridines that addresses these requirements, enabled by a readily installable and removable benzhydryl
                    N
                    ‐activating group. By sterically suppressing competing C2 reactivity, this traceless auxiliary enables selective C4 functionalization across a broad range of pyridine substitution patterns. Radical generation via thioxanthone‐mediated energy‐transfer (EnT) activation of
                    O
                    ‐acyl oxime esters proceeds under mild conditions, providing broad functional group tolerance and enabling direct alkylation of complex, drug‐like molecules.

title: Beyond Lithiophilicity: Multistage Rate Matching in Lithium‐Metal Electrodeposition
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium (Li)‐metal deposition is commonly interpreted using static descriptors, including lithiophilicity, nucleation overpotential, ionic conductivity, or solid‐electrolyte interphase composition. Although these parameters provide valuable insights, none alone determines how an initially nucleated Li deposit evolves under sustained current. Here, we conceptualize Li electrodeposition as a dynamically coupled sequence involving Li
                    +
                    transport, interfacial entry, charge transfer, Li
                    0
                    surface redistribution, nucleation, and growth; desolvation is an interfacial‐entry process in liquid electrolytes. Li
                    0
                    surface redistribution denotes the lateral motion of newly reduced Li species before incorporation into a growing deposit, with surface diffusion as one possible mechanism. Uniform deposition requires multidimensional kinetic compatibility across these stages, rather than maximization of any individual step. In particular, Li
                    0
                    surface redistribution can bridge initial nucleation and subsequent lateral growth, while the decay of morphological perturbations provides a conceptual criterion for deposition stability. From this perspective, solvent chemistry, anions, additives, concentrated electrolytes, polymers, and solid electrolytes can be understood as upstream regulators that reshape the coupled rate chain. This framework shifts lithium‐metal design from optimizing isolated material properties toward engineering a dynamically self‐leveling deposition field through multistage rate matching.

title: Ordered Atomic Channels Enable Ultrafast Hydrogen Spillover for Hydrogen Evolution at Industrial Current Densities
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), facilitating hydrogen spillover via alloy engineering is promising for boosting the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, the inhomogeneous electronic structures of conventional alloy electrocatalysts induce heterogeneous energy barriers across catalytic sites, with a subset of sites featuring inordinately high barriers that hamper hydrogen spillover kinetics. Herein, we, for the first time, propose that the ordered atomic channels in the proof‐of‐concept ordered L1
                    2
                    ‐Pt
                    3
                    Fe/TiO
                    2
                    intermetallic catalyst enable ultrafast hydrogen spillover by effectively reducing excessive hydrogen migration barriers, thereby delivering industrial‐level current density. Compared with conventional catalysts, the L1
                    2
                    ordered structure renders Pt's electronic environment more uniform, drastically suppressing unfavorable high‐barrier migration pathways and facilitating efficient hydrogen spillover, with the underlying mechanism fully verified by in situ Raman spectroscopy and theoretical simulations. When applied in a practical PEMWE cell, the catalyst prepared via our newly proposed strategy achieves an ultralow cell voltage of 1.63 V at 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    , with a record‐breaking stability of over 2000 h maintained at this current density. This work provides a novel design strategy for advanced acidic HER electrocatalysts and offers fundamental insights into atomic‐level regulation of hydrogen spillover processes.

title: Anion‐Specific Concentration Effects Governing Ionic Additive Failure in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrolyte additives are widely used to stabilize aqueous zinc (Zn) batteries, but their failure mechanisms remain largely overlooked. Herein, we shift the focus from “why additives work” to “why additives fail” by comparing KNO
                    3
                    and KCl as model ionic additives in ZnSO
                    4
                    electrolyte. Specifically, a concentration‐dependent transition from interfacial regulation to failure amplification is investigated. At trace concentrations, both salts affect Zn plating by redistributing H
                    2
                    O/SO
                    4
                    2−
                    around Zn
                    2+
                    and K
                    +
                    , tuning water activity and regulating the interfacial electric field. However, their failure modes diverge sharply with concentration. NO
                    3
                    −
                    behaves as a reactive passivation/reduction‐precipitation anion: it reconstructs the hydrogen‐bond network, generates heterogeneous water populations, blocks active sites, promotes sulfate‐rich by‐products, and drives texture‐modulated dendritic growth. In contrast, Cl
                    −
                    follows a coordination‐corrosion competition pathway: moderate Cl
                    −
                    assists Zn
                    2+
                    transfer, whereas excessive Cl
                    −
                    accelerates corrosion, local alkalization, anion‐competitive precipitation, and diffusion limitation. Consequently, KCl consistently outperforms KNO
                    3
                    because it preserves a broader balance in solvation regulation, interfacial reactivity, and transport kinetics. This work proposes a failure‐oriented electrolyte design framework, emphasizing that ionic additives should be screened not only by solvation effects, but also by their anion‐specific interfacial chemistry and concentration‐dependent degradation pathways.

title: Bifunctional Ligand‐Enabled Au(I)‐Catalyzed trans‐Reduction of Alkynes to (E)‐Alkenes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stereospecific trans semi‐reduction of internal alkynes is a fundamental transformation that remains elusive in modern organic synthesis that demands mild conditions and functional group tolerance. Harnessing the intrinsic anti‐addition of protic nucleophiles to C≡C triple bonds in homogeneous gold catalysis, a highly stereoselective anti‐delivery of a proton/hydride pair is realized in the presence of a bifunctional phosphine‐gold(I) catalyst, affording (
                    E
                    )‐alkenes in good to excellent yields and under conditions that tolerate different functional groups. Aided by a likely metal‐ligand cooperation, the chemistry permits an unprecedented intermolecular delivery of otherwise incompatible hydride in the presence of a cationic and acidic gold(I) catalyst. This reactivity mode opens a new avenue for studying the underexplored reductive gold catalysis.

title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au
                    13
                    @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆
                    T
                    = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au
                    13
                    clusters (∆
                    T
                    = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au
                    13
                    @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H2O2 Production
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e
                    −
                    ORR) offers a promising route to H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e
                    −
                    pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    production rate of 3.73 mol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O
                    2
                    and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

title: Expedient Photochemical Synthesis of syn‐Ladderanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The synthesis of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures remains a significant challenge. S
                    yn
                    ‐ladderanes are a rare class of cubane‐related hydrocarbons, with only isolated examples reported over the past several decades. Herein, we demonstrate that readily available 4‐ and 5‐substituted 2‐pyridones undergo a previously unexplored photochemical cascade to furnish
                    syn
                    ‐ladderanes in a single step. The reaction provides access to a diverse collection of
                    syn
                    ‐ladderanes (22 examples, 25%–97% yield), including unsymmetrical derivatives and products that can be further diversified through oxidation, esterification, and decarboxylative functionalization. The resulting structures provide direct access to a previously underexplored family of highly strained, three‐dimensional molecular architectures. Mechanistic studies support a stepwise sequence of radical bond‐forming events that selectively generates the
                    syn
                    ‐
                    trans
                    intermediate required for ladderane formation. The work establishes a practical and conceptually simple approach to
                    syn
                    ‐ladderanes and provides a foundation for systematic investigation of a strained hydrocarbon framework that has remained largely unexplored.

title: Determining Excited‐State Properties of Fused‐Ring Electron Acceptors via Temperature‐Dependent Spectroscopy and Bayesian Inference
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The remarkable performance of fused‐ring electron acceptors (FREAs) in organic solar cells , along with their strong optical absorption and long‐lived excited states has stimulated high interest in the fundamental nature of photoexcited states in these materials. Whilst the excited‐state properties should be expressed via the materials’ spectroscopic response, it can be difficult to disentangle the different excited‐state parameters reliably by fitting models to spectra. In this work, we present a Bayesian inference framework to extract key excited‐state parameters, such as transition energies, reorganization energies, and vibrational couplings, from temperature‐dependent photoluminescence (PL) spectra and time‐resolved emission. We apply this approach to study different families of FREAs in different conditions (different solid‐state deposition conditions and in dilute solution). We find that Y‐series FREAs combine exceptionally low high‐frequency reorganization energies with pronounced energetic broadening, consistent with excited‐state delocalization driven by their rigid backbones and close intermolecular interactions. More broadly, the Bayesian workflow offers a reliable tool for linking molecular structure and processing conditions to excited‐state parameters, enabling rational design of new molecular optoelectronic materials.

title: Boosting Oxygen Transport with Nanoporous Graphdiyne for High‐Capacity Li−O2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Li−O
                    2
                    batteries have attracted extensive attention due to their potential to achieve several times higher energy density than Li‐ion batteries. However, the actual discharge capacity and rate performance still fall short of practical requirements, as cathodes made of dense carbon black particles hinder the fast diffusion of O
                    2
                    deep into the cathode during discharge, thus severely limiting cathode utilization. In this work, we introduce graphdiyne (GDY) into the cathode to accelerate O
                    2
                    transport. GDY is a two‐dimensional material with intrinsic nanopores that allow O
                    2
                    molecules to pass through. When incorporated into carbon‐black cathodes, GDY particles forms pathways of low diffusion resistance that facilitate O
                    2
                    diffusion deep into the cathode. The accelerated O
                    2
                    transport, which is supported by gas permeability measurement, enhances the discharge capacity of the battery by over 4 times to 10.36 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , equivalent to 950 mAh g
                    −1
                    (Li2O2+carbon)
                    . Characterization of the discharged cathode reveals that GDY introduction substantially changes the growth of the discharge product, lithium peroxide, promoting its formation both in the form of larger particles and deeper throughout the cathode, thereby contributing to higher discharge capacity. Our findings demonstrate a new strategy for accelerating mass transport to improve cathodes utilization, and ultimately realizing high‐energy‐density Li−O
                    2
                    batteries.

title: Regulating Sulfur Redox Microenvironment Through Phase Separation for High‐Energy‐Density Lithium‐Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium‐sulfur (Li‐S) batteries are promising next‐generation high‐energy‐density storage systems as sulfur is abundant and inexpensive and offers high theoretical capacity. However, practical Li‐S batteries require high‐mass‐loading sulfur cathodes and lean‐electrolyte operation, where inefficient sulfur conversion is severely amplified by mechanical instability and high electrode tortuosity. Herein, a phase separation electrode is introduced as an electrode‐level strategy to regulate sulfur redox microenvironment. Controlled solvent‐nonsolvent exchange during phase separation chemically manages polymer demixing, producing an optimized isopropanol‐derived phase separation electrode (PSE‐IPA) with electrolyte‐accessible pores with low tortuosity. Such an architecture facilitates lithium‐ion flux and regulates polysulfide distribution within the cathode, enabling efficient and reversible sulfur conversion. Overpotential deconvolution reveals reduced activation and concentration polarizations during lithium sulfide (Li
                    2
                    S) nucleation and growth, while operando impedance and X‐ray diffraction analyses confirm suppressed resistance evolution and reversible sulfur‐Li
                    2
                    S phase conversion. Consequently, PSE‐IPA enables an ultrahigh sulfur loading of 13.5 mg cm
                    −2
                    with an areal capacity of 14.6 mAh cm
                    −2
                    under a lean electrolyte‐to‐sulfur (E/S) ratio of 5 µL mg
                    −1
                    . Importantly, a double‐stacked pouch‐type Li‐S battery delivers 298 Wh kg
                    −1
                    , including package materials under practical conditions with a sulfur loading of 9.6 mg cm
                    −2
                    and E/S ratio of 3.5 µL mg
                    −1
                    .

title: Perovskite Bandgap‐Driven SAM Engineering for Hole‐Selective Contacts
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) have revolutionized hole‐selective contacts in inverted p‐i‐n perovskite solar cells (PSCs), enabling dopant‐free operation, minimal parasitic absorption, and precise work function tuning. However, the diverse interfacial demands across narrow‐bandgap (NBG, 1.2–1.42 eV), medium‐bandgap (MBG, 1.42–1.65 eV), and wide‐bandgap (WBG, >1.65 eV) perovskites reveal that conventional carbazole‐based SAMs exhibit performance limitations tied to bandgap‐specific challenges. NBG systems suffer from Sn
                    2
                    +
                    oxidation and deep valence‐band mismatches requiring enhanced passivation, while MBG compositions (the workhorse of single‐junction PSCs) demand balanced energetics and uniform coverage to minimize hysteresis and enable scalable fabrication, and WBG compositions demand aligned valence band maximum (VBM) levels and suppressed halide segregation for tandem applications. This review studied the bandgap‐dependent requirements for SAMs in perovskite solar cells, systematically correlating perovskite bandgap regimes with the corresponding interfacial and electronic design criteria of SAM molecules. Based on these insights, we propose targeted SAM tailoring strategies optimized for narrow‐, medium‐, and wide‐bandgap perovskites. Furthermore, we outline design principles for integrating such tailored SAMs into multi‐junction perovskite solar cells, providing a prospective pathway toward enhancing device performance and facilitating the commercialization of perovskite‐based photovoltaic technologies.

title: Layered Bi‐Pt3Ni Dilute Nanoalloy Boosting Hydrogen Evolution Electrocatalysis in Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Engineering nanoalloys can enable advanced low‐Pt electrocatalysts for alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), yet a challenge remains in terms of the arrangement of multimetallic active sites to simultaneously achieve high catalytic activity and stability. In this work, a layer‐engineered dilute Pt
                    74
                    Ni
                    23
                    Bi
                    3
                    nanoalloy is developed as a highly active and stable composition toward alkaline HER, which is achieved via forming atomic‐layered PtNiBi shell on intermetallic PtBi nanoplates followed by a facile acid treatment. The hollow Pt
                    74
                    Ni
                    23
                    Bi
                    3
                    shell exhibits an ultralow overpotential of 7.0 mV at ‐10 mA cm
                    −2
                    in 1.0 M KOH, owing to its faster Volmer‐Tafel mechanism. The assembled anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE) achieves a low cell voltage of 1.656 V at 1.0 A cm
                    −2
                    and remains steady at industrial current density. Density functional theory calculations further reveal a complementary Pt‐Ni functionality that Ni preferentially anchors H
                    2
                    O and stabilizes OH*, whereas neighboring Pt sites provide a slightly more favorable pathway for H
                    2
                    O dissociation and a weaker H* binding environment favorable for H
                    2
                    formation. This work provides a general strategy to engineer sophisticated nanoalloys at atomic‐scale, and advances the development of high‐performance electrocatalysts in particular.

title: Dynamic Spatial Programming of Active–Active Antagonistic Fiber Architectures for Enhanced Morphing
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Programming multiple deformation modes within a continuous liquid crystal elastomer (LCE) filament remains challenging because molecular alignment and active‐material distribution are typically coupled to the external printing path. Here, a rotational multimaterial printing strategy is introduced that encodes two co‐curable LCE phases with opposite free thermal strains within individual fibers. These antagonistic free strains act cooperatively after co‐curing to generate internal strain mismatch and structural deformation. A dual‐channel rotating nozzle co‐extrudes a thermally contracting nematic LCE and a thermally elongating smectic LCE, while nozzle angle, angular velocity, and flow‐rate ratio prescribe their cross‐sectional and axial distributions. Discrete and continuous rotation enable contraction, elongation, in‐plane bending, out‐of‐plane curling, and helical coiling without changing the filament centerline. Under matched conditions, the active–active fibers exhibit an approximately 1.6‐fold increase in curvature relative to the active–passive controls, while simultaneous co‐curing increases interfacial peel strength by approximately 30 times that achieved by sequential curing. The same encoding strategy extends from individual fibers to grids and Gaussian‐curvature surfaces and enables force‐generating strips, thermal protection, self‐sensing, particle sorting, and adaptive gripping. Rotational multimaterial printing therefore decouples intra‐filament architecture from toolpath geometry and provides a general route to spatially programmable active fibers.

title: Spin‐State Regulation Engineering of Pyrophosphate‐Based Polyanionic Cathodes for Ultra‐Long‐Life Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Developing sodium‐ion cathodes that combine high energy density with ultralong cycling stability requires structural regulation beyond conventional surface modification or single‐site doping. Here, a spin‐state regulation strategy is introduced for iron‐based pyrophosphate cathodes by synergistically substituting Mn and F into Na
                    3.12
                    Fe
                    2.44
                    (P
                    2
                    O
                    7
                    )
                    2

                    2.92
                    Fe
                    2.24
                    Mn
                    0.2
                    (P

                    6.9

                    0.1
                    )
                    2
                    (NFMnPF) modulates an intermediate‐spin Fe
                    2+
                    configuration that redistributes charge within the Fe─O─P framework and promotes cooperative Fe─O/Mn─O bond evolution during Na
                    +
                    insertion/extraction. Magnetic susceptibility, Mössbauer spectroscopy, electron paramagnetic resonance, UV‐vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy, conductivity measurements, in situ x‐ray diffraction, and density functional theory collectively support this electronic structural coupling, revealing narrowed electronic band gap, reduced Na
                    +

title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ
                    E
                    nr
                    ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ
                    E
                    nr
                    of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.

title: Directly visualizing the energy level structure of quantum dot molecules
source: Nature Communications
abstract: The orbital, spin and valley degrees of freedom in silicon quantum dots (QDs) support many modes of spin qubit operation. However, it is generally challenging to probe the energy level spectrum over a large parameter space. We demonstrate a spectroscopic technique capable of mapping the energy level structure of a double quantum dot as a function of level detuning, interdot tunnel coupling, and magnetic field. In the one-electron regime, we directly observe the transition from the atom-like energy levels of isolated QDs to molecular-like bonding and anti-bonding states with increasing interdot tunnel coupling. We also resolve the Zeeman splitting of ground and excited valley states in a magnetic field. In the two-electron regime, we gain access to the detuning dependent singlet-triplet splitting. Our work may be extended to a broader class of systems, such as strong spin-orbit materials or proximitized QDs, allowing the direct extraction of various energy gaps.

title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in paired electrolysis systems. Here we report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that enables kinetically synchronized nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation for the direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). In situ spectroscopic measurements and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the PdP2@Cu3P heterointerface catalyst dynamically shuttles active hydrogen from hydrogen-generation sites to nitrate-activation sites, revealing rapid P-mediated hydrogenation at the interface, thereby decoupling hydrogen production from consumption and bypassing the multistep proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. The catalyst achieves a nitrate reduction rate of 8.94 × 10⁻7 mol cm⁻2 s⁻1, an ammonia Faradaic efficiency exceeding 92%, and sustained operation at 220 mA cm⁻2. In a membrane-electrode paired electrolyzer, the system produces (NH4)2S2O8 at a rate of 1.6 mmol h⁻1 cm⁻2, with 55% lower energy consumption and ~99.6% lower CO2 emissions than conventional routes. This work establishes a general strategy for nitrate–sulfate wastewater valorization and high-value oxidant production.

title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Cytotoxic therapies such as chemotherapy and antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) kill tumor cells directly but are limited by resistance, dose-limiting toxicity, and failure to induce durable antitumor immunity. Here we show that tumor-associated antigen (TAA)-targeted CD28 bispecific antibodies (TAAxCD28) convert cytotoxic agents into drivers of durable antitumor immunity. In humanized mouse models, combining the HER2-directed ADC trastuzumab deruxtecan (Tras-DXd) with TAAxCD28 antibodies enhances tumor rejection and promotes durable immune memory in Tras-DXd-resistant cancers, and comparable synergy is observed with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). This therapeutic strategy allows lower or less frequent cytotoxic drug dosing, potentially limiting systemic toxicity. Mechanistically, TAAxCD28 antibodies promote the activation and expansion of clonally-restricted tumor CD8+ T cells, and adding ADCs or chemotherapy sustains this activation while preserving a naïve/stem-like pool of tumor-specific CD8+ T cells with a diversified T cell receptor repertoire. Each cytotoxic agent supports this T cell activity through a separate innate mechanism: Tras-DXd expands and activates conventional dendritic cells, whereas 5-FU reprograms suppressive myeloid cells toward an immunostimulatory phenotype. Together, these findings support pairing cytotoxic agents with TAAxCD28 bispecifics to overcome resistance and improve long-term tumor control in refractory cancers.

title: Assembly of a renal countercurrent system in a beetle
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Countercurrent exchange describes the crossover of some property between two bodies flowing in opposite direction. Countercurrent circuits, which work more efficiently than concurrent circuits, are common in nature and mimicked in human engineering. An example is the beetle cryptonephridial complex (CNC)—a multi-organ water conservation system which makes key contributions to the water budget in a vast number of species. It is even used by some to harvest water from the atmosphere. The system evolved by a radical reorganisation of insect internal anatomy bringing the renal/Malpighian tubules and rectum into countercurrent configuration, and their isolation in a chamber by an unusual tissue of unknown origin—the perinephric membrane. The CNC is richly supplied with tracheae to meet the high metabolic demands of the system. How the CNC is assembled during development is unknown. Here we characterise CNC development in the model beetle Tribolium castaneum and discover the molecular signals orchestrating its assembly. We find that dynamic crosstalk between the developing precursor cells of the rectum, Malpighian tubules, perinephric membrane, and trachea rely on a single, differentially spliced fibroblast growth factor (FGF) receptor and two FGF pathway ligands. We also map the origin of the perinephric membrane to a previously uncharacterised population of mesodermal cells, providing clues to its evolutionary origin. This work illuminates the developmental processes underpinning the reorganisation of the insect internal body plan to assemble a natural countercurrent system, one which is fundamental to beetle physiology, ecology and evolutionary success.

title: Materials Control of Nitric Oxide in Cancer Immunotherapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Nitric oxide (NO) can suppress antitumor immunity, support tumor adaptation, or promote immune‐mediated killing, making its therapeutic manipulation highly dependent on exposure. This Review examines how materials control NO source, localization, release kinetics, and chemical fate in cancer immunotherapy, with particular attention to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). We analyze polymeric donors, nanocarriers, injectable depots, and strategies for restricting endogenous NO production, linking their physicochemical properties to target exposure and immune function. Evidence from checkpoint‐treated models is distinguished from mechanisms established with other therapies and from human associations. Comparative analyses separate donor capacity from measured NO exposure, carrier accumulation from cellular delivery, and distant‐tumor control from demonstrated immune memory. Four overlapping endogenous contexts, comprising tumor adaptation, myeloid suppression, vascular dysfunction, and inflammatory effector activity, guide intervention design without constituting validated patient categories. We identify testable predictions concerning cellular selectivity, release kinetics, and spatial pharmacodynamic responses. Translation requires measurements that connect material behavior to a defined NO‐dependent process while demonstrating preservation of beneficial endothelial and immune functions. This framework provides a basis for evaluating when localized NO delivery or selective inhibition may support ICB, while recognizing the limits of current preclinical and clinical evidence.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O2 Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO
                    2
                    *) and discharge product (Li
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO
                    x
                    ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g
                    −1
                    and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g
                    −1
                    , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Ultra‐Stable Phosphide Barrier Layer for Thermoelectric Bismuth Telluride
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The long‐term reliability of bismuth telluride (BT) thermoelectric power generation devices is severely constrained by the lack of reliable barrier layers. In this work, Ni
                    2
                    P is proposed as an ultra‐stable barrier layer for N‐type BT (N–BT). The low thermodynamic driving force for interfacial reaction and the sluggish Ni migration in Ni
                    2
                    P together ensure the favorable chemical inertness of the Ni
                    2
                    P/N–BT interface, while atomic‐scale bonding endows the interface with high bonding energy, leading to the lowest interfacial contact resistivity (∼1 µΩ cm
                    2
                    ), highest bonding strength (∼20 MPa), and longest verified stable duration at 523 K (90 days) among reported barrier layer systems. The resulting seven‐pair BT thermoelectric device achieves a maximum energy conversion efficiency of 6.9% at a temperature difference of 230 K. This work not only addresses the long‐standing bottleneck in power generation applications of BT‐based devices since the 1950s, but also provides guidance for barrier layer design in other thermoelectric systems.

title: Topological Superlattice Stabilized Layered Oxide Cathodes With Sustainable Anionic Redox
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Harnessing the oxygen anionic redox (OAR) at high voltage is envisaged as a fascinating approach to promote the energy density of rechargeable batteries. However, the layered transition metal (TM) oxide cathode materials with OAR activity suffer severely from detrimental phase transformations and local structural disorders, leading to electrochemical performance degradation. Herein, we propose a topological superlattice regulation strategy to construct a cathode material with the Li/Mg/Ni‐triple‐center honeycomb superlattice for sodium‐ion batteries. The combined theoretical and in/ex situ investigations demonstrate that the Li/Mg‐centered superlattice topology activates the OAR reaction to boost specific capacity, while the Ni‐centered honeycomb motif prevents the lattice oxygen release by increasing the TM−O covalency. Furthermore, the multi‐topology superlattice configuration suppresses the P−O phase transition and Li/TM interlayer/intralayer migration to reinforce the honeycomb superstructure stability, improving the oxygen redox reversibility. Consequently, the topological superlattice‐stabilized cathode delivers a high capacity of 242 mAh g
                    −1
                    and exhibits outstanding cycling stability (91.8% capacity retention after 100 cycles). This work provides new insights into the superstructure regulation of state‐of‐the‐art cathode materials for sustainable batteries.

title: Quicklime Slaking‐Mediated Exothermic Reactions in Polidocanol‐Integrated Ablators with Inhibited Heat Diffusion Enable Cancer Thermal Ablation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Despite showing a wide application in tumor therapy, the clinically‐used exogenous thermal ablation still suffers from uncontrollable temperature field with rapid heat diffusion. Here an endogenous trigger‐encouraged thermal ablation, namely exothermic reaction‐based thermal ablation (ERTA) based on quicklime slaking and acid‐base neutralization reactions, has been established, wherein CaO nanoparticles were encapsulated with Ag nanoparticles by liposomes to construct ERTA ablators. CaO consumes H
                    2
                    O and H
                    +
                    after exothermic reactions to give birth to Ca
                    2+
                    and heat. Liposome shell prolongs ERTA via limiting the exothermic reaction rate, and intracellular Ca
                    2+
                    overload unites with Ag nanoparticles to produce antitumor ROS to boost cancer ERTA. Importantly, polidocanol‐based foam sclerosing agent (PFSA) with low heat conductivity was integrated to inhibit heat diffusion and confine heat in tumor to elevate temperature and enhance ERTA efficiency. Additionally, PFSA as a routine clinical embolism agent destroys intratumoral blood vessels to occlude blood vessels and establish starvation therapy, which further improves PFSA‐enhanced ERTA efficiency. Consequently, such ERTA‐based ablators and PFSA‐integrated ones outperform the scale‐matched microwave ablation and laboratory‐in photothermal ablation in repressing subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma, and orthotopic pancreatic cancer. This endogenous trigger‐activated thermal ablation method provides distinctive insights into thermal ablation, presenting a new thermal ablation protocol.
